evidence.storage: Local archive, outside Git; all listed parts must be copied together.

30.body:
## Incremental layout experiment X5

Retain the formatting-context tree across edits, re-prepare changed paragraphs, and propagate layout only as far as changed outputs require. The experiment tests whether this path meets the latency and full-build overhead criteria in `research/investigations/incremental-layout/DESIGN.md` while preserving full-build output exactly.

Draft; recovery and implementation are in progress. The owner approved Q67–Q73 in the current handoff. Q77–Q82 remain open recommendations being implemented locally (listed below). Approval of these decisions is separate from approval of a revision to merge. The owner will merge; this PR has not been marked ready.

## Criteria

1. A paragraph edit takes under 1 ms at four workers and under 1/100 of the full stage on the same workload and environment.
2. Changing the root font size costs no more than 1.2 times a full layout stage.
3. Full construction with incremental bookkeeping stays within 5% of the baseline.
4. Every edited retained dump equals a full rebuild byte for byte, with independent reparse checks and falsifiers as specified in the investigation.

## Current branch state

- This PR's branch, `research/incremental-layout`, is at `ebd4796462efdabdb4fd6af2fa69239459981671`: steps 1, 2, 3, 3b, 3c and 4a. Step 3c has been integrated after the complete gate passed on this revision.
- The pushed `x5/step3c` branch contains the re-stack cutoff, deferred positioned flex/grid children and faster fragment splitting. Its recovery measurements and exact new font provenance are in [step3c.txt](https://github.com/mbbill/Snowghost/blob/x5/step3c/research/investigations/incremental-layout/runs/step3c.txt) and [step3c-fonts.json](https://github.com/mbbill/Snowghost/blob/x5/step3c/research/investigations/incremental-layout/runs/step3c-fonts.json). These changes are now included in this PR branch; the experiment's remaining failures and incomplete checks are preserved.
- Step 4b is implemented locally at renderer revision `f11165df08818ff0d0b7f2be7bb79a1ccc465bc7`. Its sequential/four-worker mini cases and complete ECMA-262 identity comparisons pass. Formal ECMA criterion 2 **fails** at four workers: all 20 root-font edits exceed 1.2 (independent best-of-three ratios 1.202939–1.344708); sequential passes. The remaining pages and final gate/review are outstanding. This code is not yet on the remote PR head.
- Step 5's stable NodeId style references and attribute ownership, context-owned generated bytes, walk checkpoints and source-local routing have a compiler-accepted prerequisite checkpoint. Consuming child-list updates, owned source candidates, prepared-paragraph reuse and sparse route replacement are now connected locally. Their combined module is not accepted: source-form defects were repaired, and counter checkpoint restoration exposes the runtime-window construction gap in Q82. Structural runtime correctness has not been established.
- The local structural candidate `261cfcdc290d858b01523d6eba3a64b40c91bd63` now reports actual source construction, whole-source claiming, prepared-paragraph reuse, route stores/changed records and growth copies. Source copies keep their independent loop; counting does not introduce per-slot recursive calls. The primary ran all 55 child-protocol controls on this integrated revision: malformed/missing/duplicate records and inconsistent cross-run counters reject. These are protocol checks only; the combined renderer remains uncompiled and unexecuted.
- Step 6, the final review and the final design-tree/log handoff remain outstanding.

## Recovery validation

These are new Apple M1 Pro/macOS measurements with 47 versioned Debian font files. They do not reproduce the earlier Linux font dataset. ECMA-262 and HTML5 inputs match their original pinned hashes; the original Apollo HTML and modules stylesheet have not been recovered. Historical three-page results remain in the existing run records and are not presented as newly reproduced.

Candidate renderer: `2cda0fd0093f93f52114745ecfe21749f9fc3b49`. Baseline renderer: `acd7a80d67e42053c159aaf472ea9510e6947fd3`. Whitefoot remains pinned to `3629be153b8fdb792ffe146d21dfc3251e4f887a`; no language or specification changes.

- Sequential and four-worker timing, best of three runs per edit: every measured ECMA-262 and HTML5 word/sentence edit was below 1 ms and 1/100 of the same-host full stage. Parallel maxima: ECMA-262 word 383 µs, sentence 526 µs; HTML5 word 548 µs, sentence 508 µs.
- Full-stage overhead against main, five process runs for each external-time observation: ECMA-262 +0.93% parallel and +1.37% sequential; HTML5 0.00% and +0.82%. All measured cells are within 5%; original three-workload completion is still unverified.
- The eight complete dumps (two pages × main/step3c × sequential/parallel) agree byte for byte. The corrected two-page incremental/session invocation timed out after 1800 seconds (exit 124); partial output is not a passing check. Earlier setup failures are also preserved. A replacement scratch runner checkpoints complete process and case results, including exact hashes and exits, and explicitly distinguishes selected cases from the full suite.
- `make check` passed on the integrated PR revision `ebd4796462efdabdb4fd6af2fa69239459981671` under the host lock (124.32 s, exit 0). The font manifest's JSON, file hashes and sizes were verified, and `git diff --check` passed. This does not validate the unpushed step 4b code.
- A separately identified supplementary Apollo workload (different HTML/modules bytes from the original pins) passed all four full-dump comparisons and 240 retained word/sentence comparisons across sequential and parallel builds. Every edit was below 1 ms, and full-stage overhead was +0.83% parallel / -0.47% sequential. **Criterion 1 nevertheless fails:** only 44/60 parallel word edits and 42/60 parallel sentence edits were below the measured full-stage/100 threshold. Sessions and mini cases were not selected in that invocation. The original Apollo reproduction remains outstanding.
- The maintained shell and timing checks now reject incomplete, malformed, duplicate, refused or failed driver results and preserve earlier comparison failures. The primary independently ran 55 harness controls (13 positive, 42 negative), all with the required outcomes. These controls validate the harness, not renderer correctness.

## Local step 4b evidence

Frozen baseline `16f71904ca2ea10d24ccd4f65ef7e7f221982b56` and candidate `f11165df08818ff0d0b7f2be7bb79a1ccc465bc7` use the unchanged pinned compiler, original ECMA bytes and the same 47 fonts. The primary verified all 327 renderer files in each snapshot against Git blobs, four binary hashes against their final build logs and all measured invocations, and every input/font hash.

- 48/48 processes complete; 114/114 normalized comparisons agree. Identity mode checks retained/full dump bytes after every edit; colour updates perform zero layout work.
- Root-font update/full ratios use independently selected minima from three runs per edit. Candidate four-worker median is 1.305461; all 20 fail. Candidate sequential median is 0.188943; all 20 pass. The failed threshold has not been relaxed.
- Colour delta medians across per-edit minima: baseline 3.047 ms sequential / 3.104 ms parallel; independent comparison 119.920 ms / 216.860 ms. Full style recomputation is outside these intervals and remains nonincremental.
- Three actual background falsifiers now fail as intended: omitted presence predicate (including retained/full geometry differences), resolving currentColor before comparing presence, and comparing exact background colours. Three further pseudo/origin omission mutants hit formatting errors; those errors were repaired, but their runtime checks remain unexecuted. Compilation failure is not counted as a successful falsifier.
- A separate Whitefoot experiment confirms removable short-list call scheduling overhead on a minimal workload. Two experimental renderer binaries are built, but their runtime comparison has not run. No renderer speedup, compiler policy adoption or pin movement is claimed.
- Heavy validation is now scheduled in bounded batches with no automatic competing agent queues. Gate compiler invocations acquire and release the host lock separately; contention stops the invocation rather than starting a retry queue. Existing verified outputs are reused where their exact source/input provenance permits; function caching is reserved for diagnostic builds, outside performance evidence.

## Open decisions

- Q77: compare the background predicate actually read by inline fragment generation (currentColor or positive alpha), while ignoring exact colours. Ignoring every background change misses a dependency; comparing exact colours introduces unnecessary invalidation.
- Q78: replace temporary shared value classification with per-element independent deep comparison. Q68 originally described persistent interning; step 4a implemented a different mechanism. Both shared-table alternatives impose an avoidable insertion chain. The proposal accepts repeated comparisons and requires exact-value cases, negative controls, compiler independence evidence and unchanged criterion 2.

- Q79: store inline-style and presentational-hint records by stable NodeId, so preorder changes cannot transfer declarations to another node.
- Q80: each context owns the generated bytes its retained pieces read, avoiding dependence on a replaced style arena's offsets.
- Q81: route nodes through stable source identity and source-local derived-context paths, so rebuilding one source does not renumber unrelated context bodies.
- Q82: add a Copy-filled runtime Slots constructor in Whitefoot, allowing independent restoration directly into the initialized counter window. Balanced temporary-window composition is expressible but adds merge dependencies and repeated element transfers. The separate language draft preserves ownership, bounds, explicit generic arguments and no-heap rules; its implementation and six focused Rust tests are present, but the focused Cargo attempts stopped with lock-busy status before compilation. No compiler pin has moved.

These recommendations have local criteria and remain unapproved; none has an owner-approval log entry.

## Found along the way

- Fixed in step3c: whole-context re-stacking after local edits and the expensive fragment splitting path; existing remaining costs stay in `docs/todo.md`.
- Fixed on the recovery branch: the pinned-input hash check's macOS stdin compatibility; matching, corrupted and missing files were checked.
- Fixed locally, awaiting validation: a background-presence dependency omitted from the style delta (Q77); class attributes read by generated content; stale paragraph break widths after em-based pre-pass changes.
- Fixed and verified: investigation shell commands and timing parsing could return success after driver failures, missing edits or refusals. Strict parsing and failure propagation now pass 55 positive/negative controls without changing experimental acceptance criteria.
- Deferred/current requirements: runtime splitting costs for tiny loops, unsupported proof patterns, intrinsic-cache timing, unfilled paragraph intrinsic fields, and redundant full-width breaking beside floats remain recorded in `docs/todo.md`.
- Implemented locally, pending integrated validation: node-indexed inline-style and presentational-hint records (Q79).
- Fixed in the unvalidated structural candidate: shaping-run merging compared font-family array ranges rather than family values; equal lists at different ranges could prevent a merge and invalidate value-based cache equivalence. Focused runtime verification remains pending.
- Recorded as a Whitefoot requirement (Q82): fixed-array conversion cannot consume runtime boxed arrays, and runtime Slots currently construct only empty. The draft proposes direct full initialization rather than hiding a sequential restore in the renderer. Any later pin adoption must separately disclose the newer base's already merged language changes.

## Review

The completion review by a separate read-only agent has not run. It will cover the complete final diff, design correspondence, checks and evidence limits using `docs/review-checklist.md`. No reviewed-revision claim or readiness claim is made.

31.body:
## Status

Draft, for the owner. This is research only: no code and no design-tree node changes. The owner has approved Q74–Q76. Implementation experiments C1–C10 remain unrun until drawing and shell components exist.

## Question

What does the renderer give the shell, and how does each frame's change cross? The owner ruled the boundary in Q65: the renderer gives facts and the shell owns every policy. The incremental research tree (#29, 6.3) lists the facts. This investigation turns them into records, a delta protocol and a transport.

## Change

- **`research/investigations/contract/notes/survey.md`** covers what Chromium, Gecko with WebRender, Flutter, Fuchsia's Flatland and Android's hwui send across their boundaries:
  - how they handle identity, deltas, text and resources;
  - message sizes derived for Snowghost's pages;
  - three candidate contracts;
  - how to check that a shell policy never changes the picture.

  Every claim is marked as read from a primary source, recalled, or inferred.
- **`research/investigations/contract/DESIGN.md`** summarizes the survey. It holds the findings that bear on recorded decisions, the candidates, the decisions for the owner, and ten open questions with their criteria.
- **`docs/todo.md`** gains a Whitefoot requirement: a host module for memory shared between processes.

## Findings

- **Chunk grain.** The tree's "a chunk per context" would resend about 19 MB of glyph data per word edit on html5. One chunk per paragraph cuts that to about 0.7 KB.
- **Transport.** Whitefoot has no shared-memory host module. Its six host modules are a closed list (PRE-2). So the wording "through shared memory" in `design/processes.md` cannot be built yet.
- **Facts.** The fact table lacks hit-test and scroll-routing data, and a generation on scroll offsets, which have two writers: the shell and script.

## Approved direction

- **Q74:** one chunk per paragraph (approved).
- **Q75:** begin over a byte stream with unchanged records; move to shared memory when Whitefoot has it (approved).
- **Q76:** transactions copied into a scene the shell owns (approved), against an arena read in place or versioned snapshots.

## Validation

- Survey sources were fetched in the research session and cited by URL.
- Sizes are derived, and their assumptions are stated in survey §4.
- Nothing is measured yet. The open questions say what would measure it.
- The corresponding design-tree wording will change with drawing or shell implementation: one chunk per paragraph and initial byte-stream transport. This research PR remains a draft.
